title: RewriteLab
excerpt: An exact, deliberately small arithmetic-optimization lab for inspecting the boundary between rewrite reachability and algebraic equivalence. Enumerate the whole bounded rewrite graph, inspect a shortest proof for every reachable tree, then compare it with every polynomial-equivalent tree in the same finite grammar.

title: RiskLab: the plan you would change
excerpt: Exact finite scenario-tree decisions under static CVaR and nested conditional CVaR. A supplied tree, every full deterministic policy, every terminal probability, split boundary-atom mass and independently replayable risk certificates. Dependency-free Python 3.10+ and a separate BigInt browser inspector.
headings: RiskLab: the plan you would change
A root-optimal policy can still have a worse continuation
One tail is not a fresh tail at every node

title: RobustLab: exact linear threat-set audits
excerpt: A high clean accuracy does not certify a classifier against an explicit adversarial input budget. RobustLab makes that distinction measurable for a small class where the inner attack problem can actually be solved: binary affine scores under L1, L2 and L-infinity balls.
headings: Box intersection: an optimal witness, not a clipped candidate

title: ScanLab
excerpt: Exact affine prefix scans and input-gated state-space derivatives, with algorithmic span kept separate from real arithmetic work and floating behavior.

title: ScoreLab
excerpt: Exact policy-gradient distributions, not noisy training curves. A dependency-free finite-model laboratory for score-function gradients, reward-to-go, value baselines and variance-minimizing control variates. Full trajectory witnesses, rational means/covariances and an independently checked expected-return derivative.
headings: Matrix score controls: a full covariance certificate
A correct value baseline can make the gradient nine times noisier
Exact rational gradients at a softmax anchor
Why the optimal baseline is not the state value

title: ScratchGPT
excerpt: A NumPy GPT with hand-written autograd, a trained Shakespeare checkpoint and an inspectable exact-continuation contract.

title: SegmentLab
excerpt: A confident segmentation is not evidence that an event occurred. SegmentLab is a dependency-free Python implementation of exact offline Bayesian Gaussian changepoint inference. It retains the full finite-partition evidence and marginals, not only one best cut list.
headings: Selected results, and what they mean

title: SetGuard: classifier prediction sets with an explicit coverage boundary
excerpt: A dependency-free Python CLI/API for calibration labels plus classifier probabilities, versioned JSON artifacts and unlabeled prediction sets. This is a standard split-conformal method, not a new algorithm.
headings: SetGuard: classifier prediction sets with an explicit coverage boundary
v0.2: every inclusion has a witness

title: ShapleyLab: exact attribution for an explicit reference game
excerpt: Dependency-free Python scalar callback API/JSON CLI, 49 Python tests plus four Node/actual-Chrome tests, offline demo and Python 3.10-3.13 CI. Standard formula, no new theory.
headings: ShapleyLab: exact attribution for an explicit reference game
Counterexamples are part of the demo

title: ShieldLab
excerpt: An exact tiny safety-game inspector for hand-written agent protocols. Every synchronous fixed-point obligation, winning controller move, losing rank and branching invariant/counterstrategy graph is visible. Changing only who controls a state flips the result: one-step-safe actions need not preserve safety forever.
headings: ShieldLab: a safe next step can still lose
ShieldLab: safe waiting is not arrival
ShieldLab0.3: again is a different promise

title: SparseLab
excerpt: Sparse coefficients are easy to display as a feature ranking. But a sparse selected support may be a coordinate-descent tie choice rather than an identified property of the fitted prediction. SparseLab separates the supplied convex optimization problem, numerical optimality checks and coefficient ambiguity.

title: SpecLab
excerpt: Speculative decoding built from scratch in pure Python: output verified identical to target-only decoding on the tested configurations, with verification rounds counted exactly.

title: SpectralLab
excerpt: Normalized spectral clustering exposes a choice that a scatter plot can hide: which points are neighbors, and what their connection means. SpectralLab builds the affinity and normalized Laplacian explicitly, retains the eigenspace, normalizes every row and runs manual k-means. NumPy supplies the symmetric eigenvalue solve through LAPACK.
headings: A relaxation is not a discrete optimum

title: sre-toolkit — case study
excerpt: Dependency-free Python utilities for day-to-day SRE work: error budgets, burn-rate alerting, alert triage, and the Markdown documents an incident workflow runs on — SLO definitions, status reports, and postmortems.

title: StableLab
excerpt: Finite answer-set evidence for normal logic programs.
headings: StableLab: safe replacement, not matching answers
StableLab: every input, not every rule

title: STNLab: every implied deadline needs evidence
excerpt: For tiny hand-written AI plans, inspect every implied time difference: a tight path plus a complete schedule attaining the bound, or an explicit ray proving it unbounded. Negative cycles show exactly why no schedule exists, even away from the anchor. Removing one edge returns an alternate implication path or a complete separating schedule.
headings: STNLab: every implied deadline needs evidence
STNLab - temporal bounds with attainable schedules

title: STRIPSLab: the price of ignoring delete effects
excerpt: Classical AI planning with a tiny, fully disclosed state space: zero to six Boolean facts, positive initial/goal/precondition sets, and at most eight positional unit-cost actions. Each action has add and delete sets. The real successor deletes then adds; the relaxed successor only adds. Facts absent from a state are false, not unknown.
headings: STRIPSLab: the price of ignoring delete effects
STRIPSLab search witnesses: an actual suboptimal h-add plan
STRIPSLab availability: used does not mean necessary

title: StructGate
excerpt: An offline decoding lab that makes the difference between a legal prefix and a conditional sequence distribution inspectable.

title: SubgameLab: a threat is not a credible plan
excerpt: Root stability is not continuation credibility. This exact finite sequential multiagent workbench separates root one-node stability, full-player pure Nash equilibrium and subgame perfection, retaining complete contingent plans rather than only observed outcomes.

title: SubmodLab: a guarantee is not an optimum
excerpt: Subset selection is often described as picking the most useful or diverse data. Those descriptions can hide the objective, overlap, theorem assumptions and the gap between a greedy solution and an exact optimum. SubmodLab makes each finite decision inspectable without claiming supplied similarities have learned meaning.
